content.text:
## Slowest test

**`summarizes a full season of unique readings`** in `tests/summary.test.ts` — it accounts for **~864 ms** of the suite's **~912 ms** total. The other two files (`parse.test.ts`, `dedupe.test.ts`) each finish in ~5 ms (essentially process startup).

Measured by running each file in isolation:

| File | Time |
|------|------|
| `tests/parse.test.ts` | 5 ms |
| `tests/dedupe.test.ts` | 5 ms |
| `tests/summary.test.ts` | **864 ms** |

## Why it is slow

The test builds 24,000 entries and calls `summarize`, which calls `dedupe`:

```ts
export function dedupe(entries: Entry[]): Entry[] {
  const kept: Entry[] = [];
  for (const entry of entries) {
    const existing = kept.findIndex((e) => e.id === entry.id);   // linear scan
    if (existing === -1) kept.push(entry);
    else if (kept[existing].at < entry.at) kept[existing] = entry;
  }
  return kept;
}
```

`dedupe` is **O(n²)**: for every entry it runs `kept.findIndex`, a linear scan over the array that has grown to hold all prior unique ids. The test's `season(24_000)` generates **all-unique** ids (`sensor-0` … `sensor-23999`), so `findIndex` never finds a match and `kept` keeps growing — the worst case. Total work is `24_000² / 2 ≈ 288 million` id comparisons.

The `summarize` wrapper's `Math.max(...)` spread over 24,000 values is linear and negligible; essentially all 864 ms is the dedupe scan.

I confirmed the quadratic signature empirically by timing `dedupe` alone at increasing sizes:

```
n=3000   dedupe=14.0ms
n=6000   dedupe=43.8ms   (≈3.1× for 2× n)
n=12000  dedupe=188.3ms  (≈4.3× for 2× n)
n=24000  dedupe=827.3ms  (≈4.4× for 2× n)
```

Each doubling of the input roughly quadruples the runtime — the classic O(n²) fingerprint.

The fix, if wanted, is to dedupe with a `Map<string, Entry>` keyed by id (one pass, O(n)), keeping the same "newest entry per id" and first-seen-order semantics.
